title: Planned vs predicted date chart per goal and milestone
subtitle: Mock-ups for issue #1801: how far a goal or milestone drifts and which feature drives it. Invented data. Simple only: Detailed is unchanged. Switches: ?pc1=a|b|c, ?pc2=a|b|c, ?pc3=a|b|c, &mkdata=big, &open=1, &as=commenter. Each phone and 1512 frame has a dark PNG beside it; every HTML frame takes ?theme=dark.

decisions.name: Chart form and place
decisions.question: Which chart shows planned against predicted dates, and where does it live?
decisions.common: Every proposal reads the same dates: the due date as an open diamond, the predicted date as a filled dot, and the words late, on time or early beside them (a shape and a word, never colour alone). Each names the feature that sets the predicted date with its code, and that name opens the one feature panel, whose dates now read “Dates from engineering”. The Roadmap milestone chip’s own check or warning follows the predicted date, so a chip never shows a check beside “9 days late”. Owners and approvers change dates in the feature panel; a commenter’s change there is a suggestion. Simple only.

proposals.name: Dates on goal cards
proposals.what: On the Goal map, each goal card gets one thin line under its progress bar: the due date, the predicted date, the gap between them and a late or early word. A click opens a small panel with the same line for the goal and for each of its milestones, each naming the feature that sets its date.
proposals.why: The Goal map already shows goals over their milestones, so the dates sit where people read goals; one line per item reads at a glance, and the panel covers the milestones too.
proposals.plus: No new page or tab; the milestone lines answer 'in the milestone panel' in the same place.
proposals.cost: 0 clicks to see late or early on every goal; 1 click for the milestones; 2 clicks to reach the feature. Today: no predicted date anywhere, only the goal’s At risk pill (which is about the measure, not dates).

frames.caption: At rest: each goal card shows Due and predicted dates with 4 days early, 12 days late, or No date yet.
One click on the Paid conversions line opens its dates: the goal and M2, M4, M7, each with the feature that sets it.

On a phone in dark (PNG) the dates open as a sheet; the card behind it stays whole.
A commenter opens the same dates, with “You can suggest dates; Avery Stone decides” (Avery Stone is F-107’s Decider).
The commenter’s F-107 panel: every field has Suggest a change, plus Suggest a dependency and Suggest a feature that needs it.

proposals.name: Weekly drift on Roadmap
proposals.what: The Roadmap’s goal card carries a small line of the predicted date week by week against the flat due date, with late or early beside it; one click opens the weeks. Each milestone’s own Roadmap card (opened from its chip) shows its due and predicted dates and the feature that sets them.
proposals.plus: Shows when the slip began, not only how big it is.
proposals.cost: 0 clicks for the trend on each Roadmap goal card; 1 click for the weeks; milestones only in their own Roadmap card, 1 click each. Today: no predicted date anywhere, only the goal’s At risk pill (which is about the measure, not dates).

proposals.name: Slip on milestones
proposals.what: No line for the goal: each milestone in the Goal map’s strip carries its slip in words on its own line (9 days late, 2 days early); one click opens that milestone’s dates and the feature that sets them.
proposals.plus: Points straight at the milestone that slips.
proposals.cost: 0 clicks to see each milestone’s slip; 1 click per milestone; 2 to reach the feature; the goal itself has no line. Today: no predicted date anywhere, only the goal’s At risk pill (which is about the measure, not dates).

One click on M4’s 9 days late opens its due and predicted dates.
The pointer is on F-108 Pricing page test, which sets M4’s date.
That click opens F-108’s panel, its dates from engineering.
The hard case at 1512: four milestones in the strip, each slip on its own line under its name.
M4 opened at 1512; the fifteen new features sit below the map.
On a phone in dark (PNG): the strip snaps to the Paid conversions card, whole; each slip sits on its own line under its milestone, and M4’s dates open as a sheet.

decisions.name: What predicted says
decisions.question: What is the predicted date read from, and how are its confidence and reason shown?
decisions.common: Every proposal shows late, on time, early, or No date yet with a word and a shape, and labels both dates (“Due Dec 31 · predicted Jan 12”). The reason sits behind an (i) or a tooltip, never a paragraph. None reads the feature panel’s Confidence field: it is about the feature’s effect on the goal, not its dates. All are drawn on the Goal map’s goal cards.

proposals.name: Latest end, (i) why
proposals.what: The predicted date is the latest end date among the goal's features. The card shows the date and late or early; the (i) in its panel says what it is read from, which feature ends last, and how many features have an end date.
proposals.why: It is the rule a person can check by hand from the feature panels, and the count of undated features says how far to trust it.
proposals.plus: Uses only the end dates the Roadmap already has.
proposals.cost: 1 click for the dates, 1 more on the (i) for why: 2 clicks. Today: no predicted date anywhere, only the goal’s At risk pill (which is about the measure, not dates).

frames.caption: At rest: one goal 4 days early, one 12 days late, one with No date yet.
The Paid conversions dates with the (i) open below the panel: read from the latest feature end date, F-107 ends Jan 12, 4 of 5 features have an end date.
The pointer is on F-107, the feature that ends last; the (i) stays open below.
F-107’s panel opens with Dec 16 – Jan 12, the same end as the prediction, and Milestone M7.
The hard case at 1512: the card reads Due Feb 28 · predicted Mar 9, 9 days late.
Its dates at 1512: four milestones, 2 of 20 features with no end date.
On a phone in dark (PNG) the same (i) sits in the sheet.
A commenter sees the same dates and “You can suggest dates; Avery Stone decides”.
The commenter’s F-107 panel: each field has Suggest a change, so a date change is a suggestion.

proposals.name: Range from past slips
proposals.what: The predicted date is a range: the latest feature end date widened by how far past features slipped (outcome records, avg +6 days) and by features with no end date. The card, each milestone row and the late words all show the range (5–19 days late).
proposals.plus: Confidence is drawn, not just said.
proposals.cost: 0 clicks to read the range on the card; 2 clicks for why. A range is harder to quote than one date. Today: no predicted date anywhere, only the goal’s At risk pill (which is about the measure, not dates).

F-107’s panel opens, dates from engineering, Milestone M7.

proposals.name: Status mark and word
proposals.what: The card shows a mark (check, warning, dash) and its word beside the due date; one click opens the two dates and the feature that sets them.
proposals.plus: The quietest card; nothing new to learn.
proposals.cost: 1 click on the mark to read the dates, 1 more for the feature. The card carries two pills: At risk (the measure) and the date word. Today: no predicted date anywhere, only the goal’s At risk pill (which is about the measure, not dates).

One click on the warning: 12 days late, due Dec 31, predicted Jan 12.
The pointer is on F-107 Partner referral channel.
F-107’s panel opens, Milestone M7.

decisions.name: Twenty features, four milestones
decisions.question: How does a goal with twenty features and four milestones stay readable at 1512 and on a phone?
decisions.common: Every proposal opens from the goal card’s one line, uses the app’s pass, warn and crit colours with a shape and a word for each, works in light and dark, and keeps the panel inside the window with its own scroll. The Goal map behind shows the same twenty features (fifteen not on a track yet) and M9.

proposals.name: One line per milestone
proposals.what: The panel shows the goal's line, then one line per milestone, each naming only the one feature that sets its date; the count of undated features closes it.
proposals.why: Four milestones fit without scrolling at 1512; the reader sees which milestone slips and which feature to open, and twenty features never crowd the view.
proposals.plus: Same look as the small case, so nothing new to learn.
proposals.cost: 1 click shows all four milestones, 1 more opens the feature; scrolls inside the sheet on a phone. Today: no predicted date anywhere, only the goal’s At risk pill (which is about the measure, not dates).

The commenter’s F-108 panel: each field has Suggest a change, so a date change is a suggestion.

proposals.name: Every feature a tick
proposals.what: Each milestone line also carries a small tick for every feature's end date; the feature that sets the date is a thick tick and is named.
proposals.plus: Shows the spread: one late outlier or many late features.
proposals.cost: 1 click; reading twenty ticks takes longer than four lines. Today: no predicted date anywhere, only the goal’s At risk pill (which is about the measure, not dates).

frames.caption: At rest: the goal card’s line carries a tick for each dated feature.

proposals.name: Ranked by days late
proposals.what: Instead of milestone lines, the panel ranks the features by how many days past their own milestone’s date they end, with a bar each; six show, Show all lists the twenty.
proposals.plus: Answers 'what do we fix first' directly.
proposals.cost: 1 click for the top six, 1 for all 20, 1 to open a feature: 3 clicks. Milestones are not drawn. Today: no predicted date anywhere, only the goal’s At risk pill (which is about the measure, not dates).
